title: From schedule to payroll: nine distinct checkpoints
summary: Read left to right, then follow the arrows. Every stage keeps its own status and responsible role.
steps: Complete reviewed setup and generate the employee-days expected in the range.
Preview, resolve exceptions and import eligible attendance as drafts.
Obtain supervisor review, then separate payable decisions.
Close the attendance period, stage the approved inputs and obtain independent incidence checking before the normal payroll run.
checkpoint: An import success message is not an attendance approval, a period close or a completed payroll run.

title: Prepare masters, review them, then assign effective coverage
summary: Work from the employee and schedule masters toward one reviewed roster and policy for each work date.

nodes.label: Coverage report
nodes.detail: HR · find missing or ambiguous dates

steps: Confirm employee identity and supervisor routing before assigning a schedule.
Prepare draft roster/policy versions and obtain the required independent review.
Create and approve effective roster, policy and legal-regime assignments.
Use the coverage report to resolve gaps or overlaps, then generate expected days.
checkpoint: Active is not the same as approved. Missing or ambiguous effective coverage must be resolved before processing.

title: A five-day rotation with an overnight third shift
summary: This is the accepted SLERPTECH IT-operations proposal. Day offsets are relative to the cycle start, not weekday numbers.
steps: Assign the appropriate team cycle and effective dates; verify the cycle-start reference.
Keep next-day checkout timestamps for night work. Resolve the work date from the reviewed schedule.
The proposal includes a one-hour unpaid break, starting four hours after shift start; continuous coverage needs break relief.
Review company applicability and night-work requirements before approval and employee assignment.
checkpoint: The diagram illustrates a proposed company rotation. It does not establish statutory working-time or night-work approval.

title: Import the ready groups while retaining exceptions
summary: Review import covers all ready employee-days in the saved batch, across pages and regardless of display filters.

nodes.label: Keep exceptions
nodes.detail: Filter, export and correct with reasons

nodes.label: Verify result
nodes.detail: Saved Draft counts and source links

steps: Upload or resume and run Preview / Refresh.
Ready groups may proceed together; exceptions remain in the batch for later resolution.
Review the confirmation counts. Filters and the current page do not restrict the all-ready import scope.
After import, compare counts and source links. Re-upload or retry uses duplicate protection rather than adding the same protected punch again.
checkpoint: No ready groups means no import to confirm. Correct the cause and refresh the preview; do not add invented evidence to make a row pass.

title: Resolve the cause of an exception, then revalidate
summary: Start with the issue category. A mapping problem, a missing assignment and a missing punch require different evidence.

nodes.label: Filter the issue list
nodes.detail: Attendance user · status and issue type

nodes.label: Open the employee-day
nodes.detail: Select the grid row to see source details

nodes.label: Identify the cause
nodes.detail: Code, dates, setup or missing evidence

nodes.label: Use the owning workflow
nodes.detail: Fix reviewed setup or supported evidence

nodes.label: Record a clear reason
nodes.detail: Keep original rows and audit history

steps: UNMATCHED: verify the employee code and selected organization; map only when the identity is known.
SETUP: resolve effective roster/policy/employee coverage through reviewed masters and assignments.
PUNCH_ISSUE or INVALID: verify original timestamps, distinct punches and the date scope; correct only with evidence.
MISSING: investigate the expected day, approved leave, holiday and source feed. No punches alone does not prove absence.
checkpoint: A correction reason explains the evidence; it is not a substitute for the evidence. Imported or reviewed records may require the formal correction workflow.

title: Find no-punch days without inventing attendance
summary: Expected attendance starts from the employee population and reviewed schedule, not from whoever appears in a CSV.

nodes.label: Choose organization / range
nodes.detail: HR · include the full intended scope

nodes.label: Classify the expectation
nodes.detail: Workday, rest day, holiday or leave

steps: Generate expected attendance for a reviewed organization/date range, up to 31 days per process run.
Check working days, roster rest days, holiday classifications and approved full/partial leave.
Compare expected days with actual recorded punches, including employees who have none.
Resolve setup and evidence issues, then process applicable recalculation and review steps.
checkpoint: Generation creates expectations and review findings. It does not create punches, approve attendance or create a payroll deduction.

title: Submit attendance, then approve it or return it for clarification
summary: The assigned supervisor decides on the submitted revision. Review approval remains separate from document completion and pay.
steps: The employee or authorized HR reviews the draft and submits it with a comment.
The assigned supervisor checks punches, evidence and the current revision.
Return a disputed record for clarification; an eligible corrected record must be submitted again.
Approval records the supervisor decision. It does not automatically complete the native document or payroll.
checkpoint: Bulk approval rechecks each eligible submitted record in the searched scope; self-approval, synthetic data and conflicts are not silently accepted.

title: A correction is proposed, approved and then applied
summary: Approving the request does not by itself rewrite native attendance. Application has its own state and consistency checks.

nodes.label: Propose complete times
nodes.detail: Include valid unchanged times and reason

nodes.label: Supervisor reviews
nodes.detail: Approve, return or reject the proposal

nodes.label: HR applies correction
nodes.detail: Recheck revision, period and payroll state

steps: Load the original employee-day and propose the full corrected timestamp list, with a reason and relevant evidence.
Save and submit the request. A returned request needs clarification and resubmission; a rejected request does not change punches.
After approval, use Apply Approved Attendance Correction for an eligible record.
The application step rechecks the current revision and period/payroll constraints, preserves the original evidence and triggers the required further review.
checkpoint: An approved request can still be blocked from application if attendance, period or payroll state changed. Use the supported later correction route when required.

title: Worked time, authorized overtime and payable overtime are different
summary: A late checkout is evidence of a recorded time, not an automatic entitlement to payable overtime.
steps: Use an eligible supervisor-approved employee-day and a reason for the requested minutes.
The assigned supervisor approves or rejects the authorization request.
HR separately reviews what is payable under the applicable reviewed policy and evidence.
Use period close, reviewed conversion and independently checked Draft incidences for payroll handoff.
checkpoint: Neither attendance approval nor overtime authorization is a statutory rate calculation or a completed payroll posting.

title: Close only after the readiness blockers are resolved
summary: Readiness checks protect the complete period, including expected days that have no uploaded punches.

nodes.label: Select attendance period
nodes.detail: Period owner · reviewed range and cutoff

nodes.label: Close with reason
nodes.detail: Cutoff and state checks still apply

steps: Select the period and run Check readiness.
Resolve every blocking item through its owning workflow, including pending corrections, reviews, calculations or payable decisions.
Recheck readiness and the cutoff before closing with a reason.
If reopening is necessary, inspect linked payroll states first; processed payroll uses a supported correction/compensation route.
checkpoint: Closed means the attendance period is controlled. It does not mean payroll inputs have been staged, checked or paid.

title: Stage reviewed quantities, then have a different checker review them
summary: The handoff creates traceable native Draft incidences. The normal payroll calculation and payment remain separate.

nodes.label: Select open payroll period
nodes.detail: Must cover the full attendance range

nodes.label: Review concept and units
nodes.detail: Regular unit or explicit OT conversion

steps: Select a closed attendance period and the correct open HR payroll period.
Review the manual quantity input concept, mapping reference, units and rounding.
Inspect regular and overtime candidates separately, including exclusions and existing source links.
Stage eligible Draft incidences and obtain independent checking; reconcile before normal payroll processing.
checkpoint: Do not manually create an extra incidence to overcome a retry or reconciliation issue. Inspect the protected source link first.

title: After handoff, preserve the original and correct through the right route
summary: First inspect whether the linked incidence is still an eligible unprocessed Draft or has already completed payroll processing.

nodes.label: Completed payroll route
nodes.detail: Use a later open payroll period

steps: For an eligible unprocessed Draft, use the supported void/reconciliation action before other period changes.
For completed payroll, preserve the original incidence and select the permitted later open period.
Enter the corrected total quantity. The compensation workflow derives the adjustment against the recorded history.
Have a different authorized checker review the compensating Draft and reconcile the final linked result.
checkpoint: Do not overwrite completed payroll history or enter a second full original amount as a manual correction.
